title: Home Services Pay Per Call: How to Run Campaigns
h1: Home services pay per call: how to run campaigns
description: Home services pay per call explained: define billable calls, match buyers to hours and caps, track sources and pay partners clearly.
faq: How does home services pay per call work?
A homeowner calls a tracked number, the call is routed to a contractor, and the publisher is paid if the call meets the agreed rules, such as a minimum duration.
What should a home services call buyer agree on first?
Agree on what counts as billable: minimum duration, allowed sources, repeat-caller handling, payout, service hours and a daily cap.
Do I need tracking numbers for each traffic source?
Yes. A separate tracking number per source lets you see which partner produced each call, pay fairly and pause weak sources.
body:
Home services pay per call works when a homeowner calls a number you advertise, the call is routed to a contractor or service company, and you are paid only if the call meets the rules you agreed on, such as a minimum duration. To run it well you need clear buyer rules, tracking that shows where each call came from, and a way to stop calls going to a buyer who is closed or full. This guide covers the steps for verticals like roofing, HVAC, plumbing and pest control.

Why home services suits pay per call

Many home service jobs start with a phone call. Someone has a leaking pipe or a broken air conditioner, searches, and wants to talk to a person. That makes a call a natural unit to buy and sell. Industry rules differ, so read the home services pay-per-call page for how the vertical fits the platform, then decide your own offer.

Step 1: Define what a billable call is

Before any traffic runs, write down what the buyer pays for. The usual building blocks are:

  • Minimum duration: for example, a call counts only after it passes an agreed number of seconds.
  • Source rules: which traffic sources are allowed and which are not.
  • Duplicate rule: whether a repeat caller within a set window is billable.
  • Payout: a fixed amount per qualified call, or a rate that varies by campaign.

Put these in writing with each buyer. Most disputes come from rules that were assumed rather than agreed.

Step 2: Match buyers to their service hours and capacity

Contractors are not open around the clock, and a crew can only take so many jobs a day. Sending a call to a closed office wastes the caller's time and the buyer's money. For each buyer, collect:

  1. Opening hours and days they accept calls.
  2. A daily cap on how many calls they want.
  3. The states or areas they serve.
  4. A number that rings a person who can book the job.

With those details you can build a waterfall: the first buyer gets the call, and if they are closed, capped or busy, it falls through to the next. See how routing and caps work in the call features overview.

Step 3: Track every call back to its source

If several affiliates or ad channels send you calls, each one needs its own tracking number so you can tell them apart. Dynamic number insertion shows a visitor a number tied to their visit, so the call can be linked to the page and campaign that produced it. Read more in call tracking for affiliates. Without this, you cannot pay partners fairly or cut off a weak source.

Step 4: Consider selling to the highest bidder

Home service calls are not all worth the same. A call for a full roof replacement may be worth more to a buyer than a small repair. Real-time bidding lets several buyers be pinged at once; the highest bid above your minimum wins, and a fall-back route handles calls nobody bids on. The mechanics are explained in how real-time call bidding works.

Step 5: Watch quality and pay partners clearly

Track how many calls are very short, how many are repeat callers, and how many your buyers say were not a fit. Review the pattern by source, not by gut feeling. When you pay affiliates, a per-affiliate rate and a downloadable statement keep both sides looking at the same numbers; the payout side is covered in pay per call affiliate payouts.

Compliance: check with your own counsel

Recording notices, do-not-call rules and consent requirements can apply to calls in this vertical, and they vary by place. This article is not legal advice. Check your obligations with your own counsel before you run traffic.

How to set this up in Insight Dial

  1. Create a campaign and choose the country or state targeting for your offer.
  2. Add each contractor as a buyer with their hours, daily cap and state rules, and order them in a waterfall.
  3. Turn on blocked numbers and repeat-caller blocks, plus the pre-transfer check, so calls to closed or unavailable buyers are avoided.
  4. Assign tracking numbers per source and use dynamic number insertion on your pages.
  5. Set a per-affiliate payout rate and invite partners and buyers to their portals.
  6. Use the guided setup checklist and the test-call tool to confirm the route before live traffic.
  7. Switch on quality grades (Good, Watch, Poor); sources sending too many short calls can be auto-paused. Alerts can go to Slack, Discord, Teams or WhatsApp.

Pricing is pay as you go: a per-minute call rate plus a monthly price per tracking number, drawn from a topped-up balance. Details are on the pricing page.
